limitations: The hierarchy is a deterministic product contract, not a preferred screen composition.
Captured pages can show visual hierarchy but cannot prove persisted workflow-model behavior.

brief.productIntent: Help a QA engineer create and maintain a living workflow model whose processes later receive executable Automated check coverage.
userJobs: Understand the project's roles, rules, entities, and processes
Model one workflow with decisions and exceptions
Inspect an Automated check attached to one confirmed process branch
protectedCapabilities: Project workflow model remains the source context
Workflow remains the central working object
Automated check and Runner source remain downstream evidence
contentTruth: Sample approval flow contains six business steps and one declined-payment exception
The Approval smoke Automated check covers four of the six steps
browser runner is the Automated check execution mechanism, not a workflow-model entity

typographyRoles: Compact grotesk for navigation and controls
Readable humanist sans-serif for business descriptions
colorRoles: Deep ink identifies the persistent shell
Coral is reserved for exceptions and failed coverage
spacingAndShape: Dense navigation paired with generous business-content margins
Small radii and restrained borders rather than floating card mosaics
componentPosture: Business workbench rather than test-run dashboard
Process model and inspector carry more weight than coverage metadata
imageryRole: No decorative imagery in the operational workbench
motionTone: Direct context-preserving navigation with restrained graph transitions

productHierarchy.invariant: Workflow meaning and structure must dominate the UI; automated-check source and run evidence may explain coverage but must not redefine the product hierarchy.

avoid: Making Runner source the global hero
Reducing the workflow to a compact metadata card
Using run status as the primary project navigation
Inventing verification, freshness, or service-health claims
